analysis.investment_thesis: Inox Green is a wind O&M services company with ROCE of 2.6% — a business structurally destroying capital while trading at 129x EV/EBITDA. Six consecutive years of net losses followed by microscopic profits (₹22-28 Cr) don't justify a ₹6,549 Cr market cap.
key_strengths: Debt dramatically reduced from ₹1,085 Cr (FY20) to ₹95 Cr (FY25) — near debt-free balance sheet
Renewable energy sector tailwind; O&M is sticky, recurring-revenue model with captive Inox Wind parent fleet
Promoter holding at 56% provides alignment and long-term commitment to the business
key_risks: ROCE at 2.6% is catastrophically below any hurdle rate — this business does not earn its cost of capital
Revenue in FY2025 (₹236 Cr) is still BELOW FY2018 (₹368 Cr) — 7-year CAGR of -6.1%; no real growth story
FY2025 net profit of ₹22 Cr is entirely dependent on ₹57 Cr 'Other Income' — strip that out and core operations are loss-making
red_flags: EV/EBITDA of 129x for a business with contracting EBITDA (₹100 Cr → ₹94 Cr) is speculative-grade valuation
FY2025 investing CF of -₹637 Cr against OCF of only ₹60 Cr — funded entirely by ₹572 Cr equity raise; massive dilution risk
Operating income declining (₹82 Cr → ₹52 Cr last 5Y) even as revenue grows — margins structurally compressing
Only 3/5 years of positive OCF; free cash flow has been negative in 4 of the last 5 years (FY21-FY24)
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Inversion first: what makes this uninvestable? Start with ROCE of 2.6% — if a business cannot earn above its cost of capital over a multi-year period, all the sector tailwinds in the world are irrelevant. Revenue peaked at ₹368 Cr in FY2018 and has not recovered (₹236 Cr in FY2025). The company ran losses for six straight years (FY18-FY23) and the "profitability" achieved in FY24-FY25 is illusory — FY2025 net profit of ₹22 Cr is smaller than the ₹57 Cr in "Other Income," meaning core wind O&M operations generated a loss on an economic basis. EBITDA is contracting (₹104 Cr → ₹94 Cr) despite marginal revenue growth, signaling cost inflation outpacing pricing power.

The balance sheet transformation is real and positive — borrowings collapsed from ₹1,411 Cr to ₹95 Cr — but this was achieved through serial equity issuances that have ballooned equity from ₹96 Cr to ₹2,020 Cr in five years, heavily diluting shareholders. The FY2025 investing outflow of ₹637 Cr (funded by ₹572 Cr in new financing) signals another expansion round, but with ROCE at 2.6%, deploying more capital will likely destroy more value. At 81x P/E and 129x EV/EBITDA, the market is pricing in a transformation that the last seven years of operating history give no basis to believe in.
